article.description: Tamika Whitmore made 11-of-14 shots for 25 points as the Liberty dished out the majority of the punishment for a physical 72-59 victory over the league-leading Sparks.
article.headline: Outsized Liberty outmuscle Sparks down the stretch
article.linkText: Outsized Liberty muscle a win away from Sparks
article.story:
NEW YORK (AP) -- Tamika Whitmore and Tari Phillips came up big against the defending WNBA champion Los Angeles Sparks. Whitmore scored 25 points and Phillips added 12 points and nine rebounds as the New York Liberty beat the bigger Sparks 72-59 in a physical game Thursday night. "They probably have the best post players in the league, but I can score against bigger players,'' the 6-foot-2 Whitmore said. "My mom is 6-foot-7 -- I've had a lot of practice.'' Becky Hammon added 10 points for the Liberty, who outrebounded Los Angeles 20-10 in the second half and 35-26 overall. Lisa Leslie led the Sparks with 16 points and Mwadi Mabika had 15. "New York did what it does best -- they flexed their muscles and took this one from us,'' Los Angeles coach Michael Cooper said. Most of the physical confrontations involved Sparks forward DeLisha Milton, who tussled with Teresa Weatherspoon early in the second half, with both players receiving technical fouls. Milton then threw an elbow on a rebound, earning her a fourth personal foul, and got tangled with Phillips as they both earned fouls. Leslie got in trouble down the stretch, too, receiving two quick fouls after a break, one on an offensive rebound and another on the defensive end. She played the final 8:08 with five fouls. "We planned to take it inside because Tari and Tamika just have it right now,'' New York coach Richie Adubato said. "Leslie has been in foul trouble lately, but we are going to take it inside regardless of who's in there. That's our game.'' Weatherspoon made two baskets to break a 35-35 tie, and Crystal Robinson hit a 3-pointer to give the Liberty a 42-35 lead. Mabika scored four quick points as the Sparks ran the break well to cut it to 46-41, but the Liberty pulled away again. "We just got outhustled for about the last five minutes of the game and that was pretty much it,'' Leslie said. "They picked it up in the second half, and that was the key.'' Whitmore was fouled while hitting a layup, but missed the free throw. Johnson, though, grabbed the rebound and hit an open layup for a 50-43 lead. Whitmore then went inside on three straight possessions, hitting one free throw and scoring on two acrobatic layups. The Sparks stayed in the game on 3-pointers from Milton and Sophia Witherspoon, but the Liberty got a jumper from Johnson, a 3-pointer from Hammond and a putback from Phillips to start a 12-2 run that pushed their lead to double digits. Phillips and Whitmore dominated the Sparks down the stretch. Whitmore's shooting and Phillips' hustle and muscle under the basket turned the tables on the defending champions. "I want them to think about me,'' Phillips said. "Yes, they are grandiose, and they have a big stature and everything like that, but when they see me, what are they thinking? "They have to bring their best game against me.''

Game notes
Los Angeles guard Latasha Byears, suspended two games for fighting with Seattle's Michelle Marciniak on July 11, did not play because of a right knee injury she sustained in that game. ... New York's Vickie Johnson was honored before the game for scoring her 2,000th career point on July 13. The pregame ceremony included footage of Johnson scoring the first basket in league history to open a 67-57 victory over the Sparks on June 21, 1997. ... During pregame warmups, both teams wore pink T-shirts in honor of Breast Cancer Awareness Night, and each Liberty player presented a pink-and-white basketball to a breast cancer survivor.
